## Security / risk notes

<!-- Anything reviewers should pay extra attention to. Public endpoints? New secrets? PII handling? -->
---CONTRIB
97:13. **Python:** Ruff (lint) → Black `--check` (format) → mypy (types) → Bandit (SAST) → pytest (from Week 8).
98:14. **Frontend:** ESLint → Prettier `--check` → Vitest (from Week 8).
99:15. **Secret scanning:** betterleaks in pre-commit hook AND in CI. A secret detected in CI blocks merge.
129:16. **SAST:** Bandit (Python) + CodeQL (GitHub Actions) on every PR. **Suppression hygiene (#806):** a suppression comment carries its test id and *nothing else* — put the justification on its own line above, and never spell `# nosec`/`# noqa` inside prose. Bandit parses everything after its token as a test-id list (so an inline explanation emits one warning per word, and merely *mentioning* the token in a nearby comment does the same); Ruff rejects the same shape as a malformed directive. **Judge a suppression by the gate's exit code, never by its warnings:** `bandit -c pyproject.toml -r backend/app/` (the CI command) must exit 0 with "No issues identified". A `nosec encountered … but no failed test` warning does **not** mean the suppression is dead — on a multi-line node bandit emits one per covered line that had no finding, so it is unavoidable noise around a load-bearing marker. Removing one on that evidence breaks the build; confirm against the exit code first.
130:17. **Dependency vulnerability scanning:** Dependabot alerts + auto-PRs for security updates, plus a synchronous CI gate (`pip-audit` backend, `pnpm audit` frontend). Python deps are pinned in `backend/requirements*.txt` (single source of truth; `environment.yml` and CI install from there).
134:## D. Coding structure & tooling
138:18. **Python runtime:** `conda` only (`conda create -n dataq python=3.13`). Not venv, not poetry, not pyenv.
139:19. **Python formatter:** Black. Config in `pyproject.toml`. CI rejects unformatted code.
140:20. **Python linter:** Ruff. Replaces flake8 + isort + pyupgrade. Config in `pyproject.toml`.
141:21. **Python type checker:** mypy (strict mode). Config in `pyproject.toml`. When adding a new typed runtime import to `backend/app/`, pin the package in `backend/requirements.txt` and add the same pin to `backend/requirements-typecheck.txt` (the typed subset CI's mypy job installs). That is the whole list: the pre-commit ruff/black/mypy hooks are `language: system` and run the conda env's copies, so `.pre-commit-config.yaml` carries no versions of its own (#2080). `scripts/run-pinned-tool.py` refuses to run a hook whose env differs from those pins, and tells you to `conda env update`, so a local pass stays evidence of a CI pass.
142:22. **Frontend package manager:** pnpm. Not npm, not yarn.
143:23. **Frontend formatter:** Prettier. Config in `frontend/.prettierrc`.
144:24. **Frontend linter:** ESLint with TypeScript rules. Config in `frontend/eslint.config.cjs`.
145:25. **Config / 12-factor:** All environment-specific config via env vars. Backend uses Pydantic Settings (`backend/app/core/config.py`). Frontend uses Vite env vars (`VITE_*`). No env-specific code branches.
149:## E. Observability & error handling
151:26. **Structured logging from Week 1.** `structlog` with JSON output. Every log entry carries a `request_id` correlation ID propagated FastAPI → Celery → GX. Configuration in `backend/app/core/logging.py`.
152:27. **PII redaction at the logger level** — not at every call site. Failed-check sample rows can contain sensitive data. The redactor in `backend/app/core/logging.py` strips known PII fields centrally.
153:28. **Consistent error shape** across all API responses. Definition in `backend/app/core/errors.py`:
157:29. **App Insights exception tracking wired from Week 1**, not Week 7. Middleware in `backend/app/main.py` captures all unhandled exceptions from the first commit; request/task spans and logs export through the vendor-neutral OpenTelemetry seam (`backend/app/core/tracing.py` + `core/otel.py` — App Insights on Azure, OTLP elsewhere).
161:## F. Database & migrations
163:30. **Backward-compatible migrations only.** No `DROP COLUMN` + code change in the same PR. Two-step deploys from Week 5 onward:
166:31. **Migration PR checklist:** rollback plan documented + "tested `alembic upgrade head` and `alembic downgrade -1` locally" ticked before requesting review.
167:32. **Read-modify-write is only as safe as its constraint.** There is no row-locking on the read-then-write paths today, so any "read current state → compute next → insert" sequence (e.g. the per-check `version_no` snapshot) can be raced by a concurrent writer. Guard each such write with a **unique constraint** (or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`), and **catch the `IntegrityError`** to surface a **409** (reload + retry), not an unhandled 500 — e.g. `check_service.update_check` on `uq_check_versions_check_version`. `get_db` issues an explicit `rollback()` on any exception so a poisoned transaction never reaches the connection's next user.
171:## G. Documentation & decision history
173:33. **ADRs in `docs/site/adr/`** for every significant architecture decision. Use the `/adr-create` skill or follow the template in `docs/site/adr/README.md`. One short markdown per decision; keep it to 1–2 pages.
174:34. **Architecture diagram in `docs/site/architecture/overview.md`** (Mermaid). When a new component, datasource, or integration is added, update the diagram in the same PR as the code.
175:35. **Local setup script** `scripts/setup.sh` — one command from a fresh clone to a working dev environment (conda env + pre-commit install + docker-compose up + `alembic upgrade head` + seed data).
179:## H. Security review cadence
181:36. **End-of-week quick scan from Week 2 onward:** review Dependabot vuln alerts, secret scan results, OWASP top-10 spot check on any new endpoints, Key Vault access audit. The `/security-scan` skill (`.claude/skills/security-scan/`) runs this checklist.
182:37. **Hard security review gate before Week 7 deploy:** full pass on all of the above plus public-endpoint exposure review (especially `/api/v1/orchestration/events/*` and `/mcp`).
183:38. **Security vulnerabilities are not public GitHub issues.** Report via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/security/advisories/new). See [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md).
184:39. **Quarterly MCP supply-chain audit:** once a quarter, for each client-side MCP server pinned in `.mcp.json` (see CLAUDE.md Appendix), verify the package hasn't been deprecated, yanked, or transferred to a new publisher (e.g. `npm view <pkg> maintainers time`), and review the changelog before bumping the pinned major version. MCP servers run with local tool access — treat a publisher change like a compromised dependency until verified.
185:40. **Dependency license guardrail ([ADR 0031](docs/site/adr/0031-oss-byol-distribution-licensing.md)):** DataQ ships MIT — the dependency tree stays free of strong-copyleft and source-available licenses (GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL/Elastic, Commons-Clause). Weak copyleft (LGPL/MPL/EPL) is acceptable with notice preservation. Adding a dependency that violates this needs an explicit ADR-level exception. Run the license sweep (backend: installed-env metadata; frontend: lockfile/`node_modules` license fields) alongside the rule-39 quarterly audit and before any release/image publish.
186:41. **Published docs (`docs/site/`, the `docs_dir` GitHub Pages build) never cite issue IDs or PR numbers** — no `#NNNN`, no `github.com/.../issues/…` or `/pull/…` links. > workflows only roll images onto resources that already exist — they never create infra. The
> `dataq-app-beat` Container App / `beat` ECS service (#1811) is the first instance of this: apply
> `deploy/terraform/azure/` and `deploy/terraform/aws/` on both clouds, set the new
> `BEAT_APP_NAME` repo variable (Azure; AWS derives the beat service name from its fixed
> `dataq-app-beat` family, same as the other services), **then** dispatch `deploy.yml` /
> `deploy-aws.yml` — dispatching first would `az containerapp update` / `ecs update-service`
> against a resource that doesn't exist yet and fail the deploy.

Migrations are additive/backward-compatible (CLAUDE.md), so the workflow runs
`alembic upgrade head` **before** rolling the apps — the running old code
tolerates the new schema. (This is exactly the dev-DB step that, when skipped,
500s the checks endpoint after a schema-adding deploy.)

Use an **immutable** `image_tag` per release — ACA caches a tag at the node, so a
same-tag rebuild won't be re-pulled on a new revision. Push-on-merge is
intentionally **off**; deploys are manual `workflow_dispatch`.

#### Docs site: release tags must be allowed to deploy Pages

The `github-pages` environment's deployment-branch policy admits `main` **and the tag
pattern `v*`** (added 2026-09-03 via
`gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies -f name='v*' -f type=tag`).
Without the tag policy a release tag still lets mike commit `docs/vX.Y.Z/` to `gh-pages`,
but the Pages deploy job is rejected and the live site never picks the version up. Re-add it
after any environment reset.

### Workspace membership: the next deploy must go through the workflow

The `workspace_members` migration and the code that reads it are on `main` in
separate steps and neither has rolled yet. The Deploy workflow runs
`alembic upgrade head` **before** it rolls images, so a normal deploy is safe in
either order. A hand-rolled image roll — `az containerapp update`, or a revision
rollback — ahead of the migration is not: the app would find no table.

The app degrades rather than failing (a missing table reads as "membership is not
enforced", with a `membership_table_missing` WARNING per process), so the
symptom is a log line, not an outage. Roll through the workflow anyway; the
fail-safe is a floor, not a plan.

## Pre-deploy checklist

Confirm the change is *ready and green* before you push it to prod:

- [ ] **Everything intended is merged to `main`** and you're deploying that known SHA (blank
  `image_tag` → the immutable commit SHA).
- [ ] **CI is fully green** on that SHA — lint, format, type-check, **all unit + integration
  tests**, the security scans (Bandit / CodeQL / secret-scan / dependency-audit), and the
  frontend E2E. The local verification battery (the same gate) passes too — don't let CI be
  the first feedback loop.
- [ ] **Docs are up to date** for what's shipping — `CLAUDE.md` §13 headline + `docs/progress.md`
  ticked; an **ADR** for any significant decision; the **env-var reference** + this deploy
  guide for any new config; and **user docs** for any new user-facing feature.
- [ ] **DB migrations are safe** — additive/backward-compatible (nullable `ADD COLUMN` / new
  table; no `DROP`/rename/`NOT NULL`-without-default in the same PR as the code that needs
  it), `upgrade` **and** `downgrade` tested locally. The workflow runs `alembic upgrade head`
  **before** rolling the apps, so old code never sees a missing column — you just confirm the
  revision is safe. *Note:* an `ALTER` on a hot table (`runs` / `results` / `pipeline_runs`)
  can block on a live-worker lock and hang the migrate job (#605); recovery + root-cause
  hardening are in [#708](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/708).
- [ ] **Migration-specific pre-deploy steps have been run.** Some revisions need a manual step
  against the live database *before* the migrate job runs, and that step lives in the
  **migration's own docstring** — not here, because it is revision-specific and would rot if
  duplicated. Before deploying, list the revisions that are pending on prod
  (`alembic current` vs `alembic heads`) and read each one's docstring in
  `backend/alembic/versions/` for a **`MANDATORY PRE-DEPLOY`** section; run what it says and

- [ ] **Config + secrets are in place** — the required GitHub env/vars and Key Vault secrets
  (see the [prerequisites](#before-you-deploy-production-prerequisites) above), especially any
  new key this release reads.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Published docs never cite issue IDs, PR numbers, or link to unpublished docs.

CONTRIBUTING.md rule 41: everything under `docs/site/` (the mkdocs `docs_dir`,
built to the public GitHub Pages site) is read by people with no access to this
repo's issue tracker. A `#1234` or an `.../issues/1234` / `.../pull/1234` link
is internal project-tracking noise to that reader — state the behavior or
decision itself, not the ticket that produced it. Bare GitHub issue/PR
shorthand is never how DataQ's own ADRs cite each other either (that's always
"ADR 0012" or a same-directory `0012-*.md` link, never `#0012`), so this check
needs no ADR-to-ADR exception.

A published page also must never link to an unpublished internal doc
(README/CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE.md, docs/progress*.md, docs/retro*.md,
docs/ops-log.md) — those aren't reachable from the site, so the link is dead
weight for a reader outside the repo.

(Minimizing an ordinary page's links into docs/site/adr/, and minimizing an
ADR's own links to the PR that shipped it, are judgment calls a script can't
make — that's a review-time check, not this one.)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

SITE = Path("docs/site")

# `#35;` alone (no lookahead: not `#(?!35;)`) is Mermaid's HTML-entity escape for
# a literal `#` in sequence diagrams (35 = ASCII code for '#'); the convention is
# documented in CONTRIBUTING.md, and a bare `#35;` is not an issue/PR reference. `#35;NNN` (the
# escape immediately followed by digits) IS
# this repo's documented convention for citing an issue *inside* that escape, so
# it's matched separately below rather than excluded outright.
ISSUE_OR_PR_SHORTHAND = re.compile(r"#(?!35;)[0-9]{2,5}\b")
MERMAID_ESCAPED_SHORTHAND = re.compile(r"#35;[0-9]{2,5}\b")
ISSUE_OR_PR_LINK = re.compile(r"github\.com/[^)\s]*?/(?:issues|pull)/[0-9]+")

# A doc name optionally followed by a `#fragment` before the closing paren, so
# `deploy/README.md#pre-deploy-checklist` is still caught. `adr/README.md` is
# excluded: that's the published ADR index (docs_dir covers all of docs/site/),
# not the unpublished root README this rule targets.
UNPUBLISHED_DOC_LINK = re.compile(
    r"\]\([^)]*\b("
    r"(?<!adr/)README\.md"
    r"|CONTRIBUTING\.md"
    r"|CLAUDE\.md"
    r"|docs/progress[^)#]*\.md"
    r"|docs/retro[^)#]*\.md"
    r"|docs/ops-log\.md"
    r")(#[^)]*)?\)"
)


def main() -> int:
    if not SITE.is_dir():
        print(f"{SITE} not found — run from the repo root")
        return 1

# Changelog

All notable user-facing changes to DataQ are documented here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and the project uses
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

**Cadence:** one curated entry per **minor/major release, written at tag time** —
not per PR. Patch releases get an entry only when the change is user-visible or
security-relevant. Raw material comes from the squashed conventional commits
(`git log v<prev>..HEAD --oneline`); curate it down to what a deployer or user
would act on. The step lives in the release checklist in
[docs/site/operate/runbook-faq.md](docs/site/operate/runbook-faq.md).

## [Unreleased]

## [1.2.0] — 2026-10-04

The DQ-intelligence and operability cycle (2026-08-22 → 2026-10-04). The curated user-facing
entry lives on the docs site — [docs/site/reference/changelog.md](docs/site/reference/changelog.md)
— and in the GitHub Release body; headlines:

### Added

- **Six SQL datasources on one engine-generic base (ADR 0045):** PostgreSQL, MySQL / MariaDB,
  Trino, Amazon Athena and Amazon Redshift, plus SQL Server / Azure SQL / Synapse / Fabric SQL
  (ADR 0044). ADLS Gen2 connections can sign in as a service principal, which also covers
  Fabric OneLake.
- **Per-check engines (ADR 0036):** Snowflake DMF, including custom DMFs, and Databricks DQX
  run in the user's own workspace, beside Great Expectations.
- **LLM assistance, off by default (ADR 0042):** SQL generation, check suggestions and
  root-cause narratives through a provider seam (Anthropic, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint,
  Snowflake Cortex), each validated before anything is saved.
- **Automated coverage (ADR 0047):** system-owned suites over the asset inventory, a review
  queue of suggested rules, and coverage and false-positive figures on the Dashboard.
- **Suites as code:** YAML suite files, `validate`, drift and `apply`, and a generated Python
  client with the `dataq` CLI, attached to each release, under an API compatibility policy.
- **A pipeline gate (ADR 0046):** `POST /orchestration/gate` lets a pipeline stage start its
  bound suites and wait for the verdict.
- **Operating a workspace:** reusable notification channels; the admin area as six pages
  with in-app membership (ADR 0043), guided offboarding and a workspace-health view; a hash
...
  and per-suite delivery config.
- **Access model:** Azure AD SSO via a generic OIDC contract (`DATAQ_AUTH_*`,
  no MSAL — ADR 0028); suite-level sharing (`owner`/`edit`/`view`); implicit
  workspace-admin (ADR 0027) with an admin control centre.
- **AI integration:** 8 curated FastMCP tools at `/mcp`, validated with the same
  Azure AD bearer token, fail-closed without auth (ADR 0008).
- **Deployment:** in-repo Terraform for Azure Container Apps (API internal,
  frontend the sole public surface), GHCR multi-arch images, GitHub Actions
  build→migrate→deploy pipeline, App Insights logs + OpenTelemetry traces.

content.content:
# Runbook & FAQ

## Release checklist

- All CI gates green on `main`; no open release-blocking issues on the current milestone.
- **CHANGELOG updated at tag time** (minor/major releases; patch only if user-visible or
  security-relevant — see the policy in
  [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)):
  curate `git log v<prev>..HEAD --oneline` down to what a deployer/user acts on, and
  mirror the entry into the GitHub Release body.
- **The Python client ships with the release.** `packages/dataq-client/pyproject.toml`'s
  version equals the tag before you push it (the workflow refuses a mismatch). The tag's
  workflow attaches the client wheel and sdist to the release; if you had not created the
  release yet it makes a **draft** — add the curated notes there and publish it rather than
  creating a second one.
- Backend image built + pushed to GHCR with an **immutable** tag (not `latest`).
- DB migrations are backward-compatible; the migrate job runs `alembic upgrade head`
  **before** the app rolls.
- Deploy via the **Deploy** workflow (`workflow_dispatch`); verify `/healthz` 200,
  `/api/v1/me` 401 (auth enforced), SPA + deep links load.
- Docs site published (this site) and linked from the README: after the tag, `/docs/<tag>/`
  and `/docs/latest/` both load. If the **Docs** workflow run sits in *pending*, an older run
  is holding the queue; cancel that one. A tag's Docs run that was *cancelled* while it
  waited did not publish: re-run it.

Full deploy steps + verification: the repository's **`deploy/README.md`**.

## Live smoke (deployed stack + harness data)

> Scale numbers are in [perf-baseline.md](../architecture/perf-baseline.md).

"""MkDocs hook: the changelog page's "Unreleased" section is rendered from changelog.d/.

The committed page carries only a marker line, so no PR edits the page between releases
and two PRs that each add an entry never conflict. The section is built here, at build
time, from whatever fragments exist — there is nothing to re-run and nothing to go stale.
A malformed fragment fails `mkdocs build --strict` the same way it fails pre-commit.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import sys
from pathlib import Path

_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
_SCRIPT = _ROOT / "scripts" / "changelog.py"
_PAGE = "reference/changelog.md"


def _changelog_module():  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("dataq_changelog", _SCRIPT)
    assert spec and spec.loader
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules["dataq_changelog"] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def on_page_markdown(markdown: str, page, config, files) -> str:  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    if page.file.src_uri != _PAGE:
        return markdown
    changelog = _changelog_module()
    return changelog.inject_unreleased(markdown, changelog.load_fragments())

# changelog.d — one file per change

Every PR that changes something a user, deployer or API client would notice adds **one
small file here** instead of editing `docs/site/reference/changelog.md`. The published
page renders these under **Unreleased** at build time; at release
`scripts/changelog.py assemble` moves them into a dated section and deletes them.

## Filename

```
<number>.<section>.md         e.g. 2395.changed.md
<number>-<n>.<section>.md     a second entry for the same number, e.g. 2440-2.added.md
```

- `<number>` — the issue the change belongs to (the PR number if there is no issue).
- `<n>` — `2`, `3`, … for further fragments of the same number.
- `<section>` — `breaking` | `security` | `added` | `changed` | `fixed`.

Only files matching this grammar (plus this README) may live here.

## Body

The bullet's text in Markdown, **without** the leading `- `, continuation lines unindented.
Lead with a bold phrase, as the existing entries do, and describe the behaviour — never cite
an issue or PR number, the page is public (CONTRIBUTING rule 41).

```markdown
**Changelog entries are collected one file per change.** A PR adds a fragment under
`changelog.d/` and the published page assembles them, so two PRs never conflict on the
changelog.
```

## Commands

```bash
python scripts/changelog.py lint                 # every fragment is well-formed (pre-commit + CI)
python scripts/changelog.py render-unreleased    # preview the Unreleased section
python scripts/changelog.py check --base origin/main   # what CI asks of a PR
python scripts/changelog.py assemble --version 1.3.0 --date 2026-11-29   # at release
```

A PR that touches user-facing paths and needs no entry carries the `no-changelog` label.
Dependabot PRs are exempt.

from pathlib import Path

_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]

def _load() -> ModuleType:
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("dataq_changelog_under_test", _SCRIPT)

    spec.loader.exec_module(module)

changelog = _load()

_INTRO = "# Changelog\n\nIntro.\n\n"
_OLD = "## v1.2.0 — 2026-10-04\n\n### Added\n\n- **Old.** Entry.\n"


def _page(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    page = tmp_path / "changelog.md"
    page.write_text(_INTRO + changelog.MARKER + "\n\n" + _OLD, encoding="utf-8")
    return page


def _frag(directory: Path, name: str, body: str) -> Path:
    directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    path = directory / name
    path.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
    return path


class TestFilenameGrammar:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("name", "expected"),
        [
            ("2395.changed.md", (2395, 0, "changed")),
            ("2440-2.added.md", (2440, 2, "added")),
            ("7.breaking.md", (7, 0, "breaking")),
            ("12.security.md", (12, 0, "security")),
            ("12.fixed.md", (12, 0, "fixed")),
        ],
    )
    def test_accepts_the_grammar(self, name: str, expected: tuple[int, int, str]) -> None:
        assert changelog.parse_name(name) == expected

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "name",
        [
            "2395.md",
            "2395.removed.md",
            "2395.Added.md",
            "abc.added.md",
            "0.added.md",
            "2395-0.added.md",
            "2395-a.added.md",
            "2395.added.txt",
            "2395.added",
        ],
    )
    def test_rejects_anything_else(self, name: str) -> None:
        with pytest.raises(changelog.FragmentError):
            changelog.parse_name(name)


class TestFragmentBody:
    def test_reads_the_bullet_text(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        path = _frag(tmp_path, "1.added.md", "**Lead.** First line\nsecond line\n")
        fragment = changelog.load_fragment(path)
        assert fragment.body == "**Lead.** First line\nsecond line"

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("body", "why"),
        [
            ("", "empty"),
            ("   \n", "empty"),
            ("- **Lead.** text", "leading '- '"),
            ("### Added\n**Lead.**", "heading"),
            ("**Lead.** fixes #2395", "cites an issue"),
            ("**Lead.** see github.com/x/y/pull/12", "cites an issue"),
        ],
    )
    def test_rejects_a_malformed_body(self, tmp_path: Path, body: str, why: str) -> None:
        path = _frag(tmp_path, "1.added.md", body)
        with pytest.raises(changelog.FragmentError, match=why):
            changelog.load_fragment(path)

    def test_only_fragments_and_the_readme_may_live_in_the_directory(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        _frag(tmp_path, "README.md", "# how to")
        _frag(tmp_path, "1.added.md", "**A.** a")
        assert [f.number for f in changelog.load_fragments(tmp_path)] == [1]
        _frag(tmp_path, "notes.md", "x")
        with pytest.raises(changelog.FragmentError, match="notes.md"):
            changelog.load_fragments(tmp_path)

    def test_a_missing_directory_is_an_error(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        with pytest.raises(changelog.FragmentError, match="missing"):
            changelog.load_fragments(tmp_path / "nope")


class TestRender:
    def test_sections_come_out_in_release_order_and_newest_number_first(
        self, tmp_path: Path
    ) -> None:
        _frag(tmp_path, "10.fixed.md", "**F10.** x")
        _frag(tmp_path, "20.added.md", "**A20.** x")
        _frag(tmp_path, "20-2.added.md", "**A20b.** x")
        _frag(tmp_path, "30.added.md", "**A30.** x")
        _frag(tmp_path, "5.breaking.md", "**B5.** x")
        _frag(tmp_path, "6.security.md", "**S6.** x")
        _frag(tmp_path, "7.changed.md", "**C7.** x")
        rendered = changelog.render_unreleased(changelog.load_fragments(tmp_path))
        assert rendered == (
            "## Unreleased\n\n"
            "### Breaking\n\n- **B5.** x\n\n"
            "### Security\n\n- **S6.** x\n\n"
            "### Added\n\n- **A30.** x\n- **A20.** x\n- **A20b.** x\n\n"
            "### Changed\n\n- **C7.** x\n\n"
            "### Fixed\n\n- **F10.** x"
        )

    def test_continuation_lines_are_indented_under_the_bullet(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        _frag(tmp_path, "1.added.md", "**A.** first\nsecond\n\nthird")
        rendered = changelog.render_sections(changelog.load_fragments(tmp_path))
        assert rendered == "### Added\n\n- **A.** first\n  second\n\n  third"

        tmp_path.joinpath("README.md").write_text("x")
        rendered = changelog.render_unreleased(changelog.load_fragments(tmp_path))
        assert rendered == "## Unreleased\n\n" + changelog.EMPTY_UNRELEASED

    def test_injecting_is_idempotent_and_leaves_the_rest_of_the_page_alone(
        self, tmp_path: Path
    ) -> None:
        page = _page(tmp_path)
        _frag(tmp_path / "d", "1.added.md", "**A.** a")
        fragments = changelog.load_fragments(tmp_path / "d")
        once = changelog.inject_unreleased(page.read_text(), fragments)
        assert once == _INTRO + "## Unreleased\n\n### Added\n\n- **A.** a\n\n" + _OLD
        assert changelog.inject_unreleased(once, fragments) == once

    def test_a_page_without_the_marker_is_refused(self) -> None:
        with pytest.raises(changelog.FragmentError, match="marker"):
            changelog.inject_unreleased("# Changelog\n", [])

    def test_the_real_fragments_render_against_the_real_page(self) -> None:
        fragments = changelog.load_fragments()
        page = (_ROOT / "docs/site/reference/changelog.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        assert "## Unreleased" not in page, "the committed page carries only the marker"
        assert "## Unreleased" in changelog.inject_unreleased(page, fragments)

        self, tmp_path: Path
    ) -> None:
        page = _page(tmp_path)
        d = tmp_path / "d"
        _frag(d, "1.fixed.md", "**F.** f")
        _frag(d, "2.breaking.md", "**B.** b")
        heading = changelog.assemble("1.3.0", "2026-11-29", page, d)
        assert heading == "## v1.3.0 — 2026-11-29"
        assert page.read_text() == (
            _INTRO
            + changelog.MARKER
            + "\n\n## v1.3.0 — 2026-11-29\n\n### Breaking\n\n- **B.** b\n\n"
            "### Fixed\n\n- **F.** f\n\n" + _OLD
        )
        assert sorted(p.name for p in d.iterdir()) == []

    def test_keeps_the_readme_and_accepts_a_v_prefix(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        page = _page(tmp_path)
        d = tmp_path / "d"
        _frag(d, "README.md", "# x")
        _frag(d, "1.added.md", "**A.** a")
        changelog.assemble("v1.3.0", "2026-11-29", page, d)
        assert [p.name for p in d.iterdir()] == ["README.md"]

    def test_refuses_a_second_section_for_the_same_version(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        page = _page(tmp_path)
        d = tmp_path / "d"
        _frag(d, "1.added.md", "**A.** a")
        with pytest.raises(changelog.FragmentError, match="already has"):
            changelog.assemble("1.2.0", "2026-10-04", page, d)
        assert d.joinpath("1.added.md").exists()

    def test_refuses_with_nothing_to_assemble(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        page = _page(tmp_path)
        (tmp_path / "d").mkdir()
        with pytest.raises(changelog.FragmentError, match="nothing to assemble"):
            changelog.assemble("1.3.0", "2026-11-29", page, tmp_path / "d")

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(("version", "date"), [("1.3", "2026-11-29"), ("1.3.0", "29/11/2026")])
    def test_refuses_a_malformed_version_or_date(
        self, tmp_path: Path, version: str, date: str
    ) -> None:
        page = _page(tmp_path)
        d = tmp_path / "d"
        _frag(d, "1.added.md", "**A.** a")
        with pytest.raises(changelog.FragmentError):
            changelog.assemble(version, date, page, d)


class TestPathFilter:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "path",
        [
            "backend/app/api/v1/runs.py",
            "frontend/src/pages/Runs.tsx",
            "packages/dataq-client/src/x.py",
            "integrations/airflow/dataq_airflow_callback.py",
            "deploy/terraform/aws/main.tf",
            "docs/site/guides/features.md",
            "docs/site/get-started/install.md",
            "docs/site/reference/api-compatibility.md",
        ],
    )
    def test_user_facing(self, path: str) -> None:
        assert changelog.is_user_facing(path)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "path",
        [
            "docs/site/reference/changelog.md",
            "backend/tests/api/test_runs.py",
            "frontend/src/pages/Runs.test.tsx",
            "frontend/src/__tests__/x.ts",
            "docs/site/adr/0001.md",
            "docs/progress.md",
            "scripts/changelog.py",
            ".github/workflows/ci.yml",
            "CONTRIBUTING.md",
        ],
    )
    def test_not_user_facing(self, path: str) -> None:
        assert not changelog.is_user_facing(path)


def _git(cwd: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args],
        cwd=cwd,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
        env={
            "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "t",
            "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "t@example.invalid",
            "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "t",
            "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "t@example.invalid",
            "HOME": str(cwd),
            "PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin",
        },
    ).stdout


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:

    (tmp_path / "backend" / "app").mkdir(parents=True)

    _git(tmp_path, "commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
    _git(tmp_path, "checkout", "-q", "-b", "feature")

def _commit(repo: Path, path: str, text: str) -> None:
    target = repo / path
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_text(text)
    _git(repo, "add", path)
    _git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", f"touch {path}")


class TestCheck:
    def test_a_user_facing_change_without_a_fragment_fails(self, repo: Path) -> None:
        _commit(repo, "backend/app/a.py", "a = 2\n")

        assert len(problems) == 1
        assert "backend/app/a.py" in problems[0]
        assert "no-changelog" in problems[0]

    def test_a_fragment_satisfies_it(self, repo: Path) -> None:
        _commit(repo, "backend/app/a.py", "a = 2\n")
        _commit(repo, "changelog.d/9.fixed.md", "**F.** f\n")
        assert changelog.check("main", False, repo) == []

    def test_the_exemption_waives_the_missing_fragment(self, repo: Path) -> None:
        _commit(repo, "backend/app/a.py", "a = 2\n")
        assert changelog.check("main", True, repo) == []

    def test_a_non_user_facing_change_needs_nothing(self, repo: Path) -> None:
        _commit(repo, "backend/tests/test_a.py", "x = 1\n")

        assert changelog.check("main", False, repo) == []

    def test_a_malformed_fragment_fails_even_when_exempt(self, repo: Path) -> None:
        _commit(repo, "changelog.d/9.removed.md", "**F.** f\n")
        problems = changelog.check("main", True, repo)
        assert len(problems) == 1
        assert "9.removed.md" in problems[0]

    def test_main_moving_ahead_does_not_count_against_the_branch(self, repo: Path) -> None:

        _git(repo, "checkout", "-q", "main")

        _git(repo, "add", "-A")
        _commit(repo, "backend/app/a.py", "a = 2\n")
        problems = changelog.check("main", False, repo)
        assert len(problems) == 1

        )

def _commit(repo: Path, path: str, text: str) -> None:
    target = repo / path
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_text(text)
    _git(repo, "add", path)
    _git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", f"touch {path}")

input.content:
## Summary

- **Changelog fragments, one file per PR, assembled at release** (from the v1.2 retro). A PR adds `changelog.d/<issue>.<section>.md` instead of editing the Unreleased list, so two open PRs never conflict on the changelog, every PR keeps its CI, and nobody merges `main` in by hand.
- **The committed page carries only a marker** (`<!-- changelog.d:unreleased -->`). A mkdocs hook (`docs/hooks/changelog_fragments.py`) renders the Unreleased section from the fragments at build time, so the published site still shows unreleased changes and nothing can go stale: there is no generated text on disk to re-run or forget. `render-unreleased` prints the same section for a local preview.
- **CI** fails a PR that touches user-facing paths without a fragment, unless it carries the new `no-changelog` label or Dependabot opened it. The steps live in the existing required job **`Secret scanning (betterleaks)`** (which already hosts the repo guards), so the `main protection` ruleset needs **no change**. `pull_request` now also fires on `labeled`/`unlabeled`, so adding the label re-runs CI instead of needing an empty push.

### Fragment grammar

```
changelog.d/<number>.<section>.md         e.g. 2395.changed.md
changelog.d/<number>-<n>.<section>.md     a second entry for the same number, e.g. 2440-2.added.md
```
`<number>` = the issue (PR number if none), `<n>` = 2, 3, …; `<section>` ∈ `breaking | security | added | changed | fixed`. Body = the bullet text (bold lead phrase, no leading `- `, continuation lines unindented), and it may not cite an issue/PR number (rule 41 — the text is published). Only these files and `README.md` may live in the directory. Rendered order: Breaking, Security, Added, Changed, Fixed; within a section highest number first, then `-n`.

### Commands (`scripts/changelog.py`, stdlib only)

| command | does |
|---|---|
| `lint` | every fragment is well-formed (pre-commit hook `changelog-fragments` + CI) |
| `render-unreleased` | prints the `## Unreleased` section (what the hook injects) |
| `assemble --version X.Y.Z --date YYYY-MM-DD` | inserts `## vX.Y.Z — date` below the marker, above older releases, deletes the fragments; refuses a repeated version, a malformed version/date, or an empty directory |
| `check --base <ref> [--allow-none]` | the branch's `base...HEAD` diff touching `backend/app/`, `frontend/src/`, `packages/`, `integrations/`, `deploy/`, `docs/site/{guides,get-started,reference}/` (minus the changelog itself and `*.test.*`/`*.spec.*`/`__tests__/`) must ADD a fragment; a malformed added fragment fails even when exempt |

### Migration of the current Unreleased section

The six bullets became `2440.added.md`, `2440-2.added.md` (ADR 0048 phases), `1661.added.md`, `1661-2.added.md` (coverage sensitivity + false-positive split), `2369.added.md` (disable a check), `1762.added.md` (promote to channel). Their text is byte-identical (verified by rendering and comparing the bullet set against `origin/main`'s section); the rendered order is now by number, so the list reads 2440, 2440-2, 2369, 1762, 1661, 1661-2 instead of the hand-kept order.

### Acceptance (issue)

- **Two PRs that each add an entry merge in either order without a conflict** — demonstrated in a throwaway repo: base with the marker page, branch A adds `101.added.md`, branch B adds `102.fixed.md`; `merge B, merge A` clean, reset, `merge A, merge B` clean. The old shape (both insert at the Unreleased line) was merged beside it for contrast and conflicts in `changelog.md`.
- **The release checklist names the assemble step** — `docs/site/operate/runbook-faq.md` (the release checklist the root CHANGELOG points to) and the pre-deploy checklist in `deploy/README.md`.

### Tests (`backend/tests/scripts/test_changelog.py`, 63 tests)

Filename grammar (accept/reject tables), body validation, section ordering + newest-first, continuation indentation, idempotent injection, assemble (placement, fragment deletion, README kept, `v` prefix, duplicate version, empty dir, malformed inputs, a previewed block is replaced not duplicated), the path filter, and `check` in a real scratch git repo (missing fragment fails, fragment passes, exemption, non-user-facing passes, malformed-even-when-exempt, `main` moving ahead does not count, a deleted fragment is not an added one), plus the CLI.

**Proved they fail against broken implementations** — seven mutations applied to `scripts/changelog.py` one at a time and restored: section order reversed (2 fail), changelog.md counted as user-facing (1), exemption ignored (1), ticket refs allowed (2), assemble keeps the fragments (2), newest-first dropped (1), re-render duplicates the block (2).

## Linked issue

Closes #2395

## Type of change

- [x] chore — repo housekeeping / tooling

## Checklist

- [x] **Manually tested locally** (describe what you tested below)
- [x] **Single functionality** — no unrelated changes piggybacked
- [x] **Conventional commit title**
- [x] **No secrets, credentials, or `.env` files committed**
- [x] **Black + Ruff + mypy pass locally** (`mypy backend/tests/` full sweep: 378 files clean)
- [ ] **Prettier + ESLint pass locally** — no frontend change
- [x] **Tests added/updated**
- [x] **`/code-review` agent review run on this PR**
- [x] **Docs / ADRs updated** — CONTRIBUTING rule 43, PR template checkbox, release checklist, deploy pre-deploy checklist, changelog intro, `changelog.d/README.md`
- [x] **Changelog fragment added** — `changelog.d/2395.changed.md`
- [x] **`docs/progress.md` — N/A** for this PR (the orchestrator updates the ledger)
- [x] **Security implications considered** — the workflow reads only `base.sha` and a boolean expression through `env`, never a PR title/body; `check` runs a fixed-argv `git diff`

## Schema migration?

- [x] No schema change

## Manual test notes

- `mkdocs build --strict` with the hook: the page renders `id="unreleased"` with all seven fragments; `render-unreleased` output's bullet set is byte-identical to `origin/main`'s Unreleased section.
- `python scripts/changelog.py check --base origin/main` on this branch → `changelog: OK`; `lint` → 7 fragments OK; pre-commit over every changed file green (incl. the new `changelog-fragments` hook, the identifier and docs-reference guards).
- The `no-changelog` label was created on the repo (`gh label create no-changelog`).

## Security / risk notes

- A fragment is published text, so `lint` rejects `#NNNN` / issue-or-PR links (rule 41) before the docs guard would see the rendered page.
- `labeled`/`unlabeled` now re-run CI (cancel-in-progress keeps it to one run); labels are a maintainer action, so this is not a new trigger surface for outside contributors.

## PR #2460 — `chore(changelog): fragments in changelog.d/, assembled at release` (Closes #2395)

https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/2460 — branch `chore/changelog-fragments`, milestone "v1.3 Week 2 — operating DataQ & the first outside user", labels chore + ci. **CI fully green** on head `bd3aa655e` (16/16 checks pass; the two "skipping" rows are the main-only `deploy` / `Publish the static demo` jobs). Not merged (orchestrator merges). All 7 review threads answered and resolved.

### Fragment grammar shipped (exact)
```
changelog.d/<number>.<section>.md         e.g. 2395.changed.md
changelog.d/<number>-<n>.<section>.md     second entry for the same number, e.g. 2440-2.added.md
```
regex `^([1-9]\d*)(?:-([1-9]\d*))?\.(breaking|security|added|changed|fixed)\.md$`. `<number>` = issue (PR number if none); `<n>` = 2, 3, …. Body = the bullet text, Markdown, bold lead phrase, NO leading `- `, continuation lines unindented (the renderer adds `- ` and the 2-space indent). Body may not be empty, start with `- `/`#`, or cite a ticket / link an internal doc — `lint` applies the four rule-41 patterns loaded from `scripts/check-docs-references.py` itself. Only grammar files + `README.md` may live in the directory. Render order: Breaking, Security, Added, Changed, Fixed; within a section highest number first, then `-n` ascending.

### What shipped (3 commits + 1 fixup)
- `scripts/changelog.py` (stdlib): `lint` · `render-unreleased` (stdout) · `assemble --version X.Y.Z --date YYYY-MM-DD` (inserts `## vX.Y.Z — date` below the marker, above older releases, deletes fragments; refuses repeat version / bad version or date / empty dir) · `check --base <ref> [--allow-none]` (diff `base...HEAD`; user-facing = `backend/app/`, `frontend/src/`, `packages/`, `integrations/`, `deploy/`, `docs/site/{guides,get-started,reference}/` minus `changelog.md`, `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `__tests__/`; a fragment counts when added OR modified; a malformed fragment fails even when exempt).
- **Unreleased rendering = a mkdocs hook** `docs/hooks/changelog_fragments.py` (listed BEFORE `llm_export.py` in `mkdocs.yml` — review found the raw-Markdown/llms-full copies otherwise snapshot the bare marker). The committed `changelog.md` carries only `<!-- changelog.d:unreleased -->`; the section is built at build time, so nothing on disk can go stale and no PR edits the page between releases. Chosen over a pre-build step for exactly that reason. `mkdocs build --strict` fails on a malformed fragment.
- `changelog.d/README.md` (grammar/example/commands) + `changelog.d/2395.changed.md`; the six existing Unreleased bullets migrated byte-identically to `2440.added.md`, `2440-2.added.md`, `1661.added.md`, `1661-2.added.md`, `2369.added.md`, `1762.added.md` (order on the page is now by number, not the hand-kept order).
- **CI**: `lint` + `check --base HEAD^1` steps folded into the existing required job **`Secret scanning (betterleaks)`** (already hosts the repo guards) — **no ruleset change needed**; verified in the job log (`changelog: OK`). Exemption: PR label `no-changelog` (created on the repo) or PR author `dependabot[bot]`. `pull_request` types now include `labeled`/`unlabeled` so adding the label re-runs CI (note: labels passed at `gh pr create` fire extra runs that concurrency cancels — benign). `docs.yml` path filters include `changelog.d/**` + `scripts/changelog.py`.
- Pre-commit hook `changelog-fragments` (runs `lint`). Docs: CONTRIBUTING **rule 43**, PR-template checkbox, release checklist in `docs/site/operate/runbook-faq.md` names the assemble step (merge the assemble PR before the tag), `deploy/README.md` pre-deploy checklist too, changelog intro sentence.
- Tests `backend/tests/scripts/test_changelog.py` (67): grammar accept/reject, body rules, ordering, idempotent injection, assemble cases, path filter, `check` in real scratch git repos (incl. merge-ref base and main-moved-ahead), CLI. **Mutation-proved**: 10 mutations of the script each turned tests red (section order, changelog.md as user-facing, exemption ignored, ticket refs allowed, assemble keeps fragments, newest-first dropped, re-render duplicates, A-only status, two-dot diff, internal-doc links allowed). Local gate: black/ruff/mypy (full `mypy backend/tests/` sweep 378 files clean), pre-commit over every changed file, `mkdocs build --strict`.
- **Acceptance**: two-branch demo in a scratch repo — A adds `101.added.md`, B adds `102.fixed.md`; merged B→A and A→B, both clean; the old same-line shape conflicts (in PR body). Release checklist names the assemble step.

### Review
`/code-review` medium (`--comment`): 7 findings, all fixed in `bd3aa655e`, none filed/deferred. Nothing left undone.

### Test DB
None created for lane `clog` — the tests use `tmp_path` + scratch git repos, no Postgres. Nothing to drop.

### Notes for the orchestrator
- Other in-flight PRs carrying a fragment will pass `check` once this merges; a PR that touches user-facing paths with no fragment will need the `no-changelog` label (or a re-run after labeling).
- The root `CHANGELOG.md` (curated at tag time, Keep-a-Changelog) is untouched and out of scope.
- `docs/progress.md` and CLAUDE.md untouched per the brief.
